## The idea

When people produce something together (a startup, a research paper, a winning season), how much of the result is each person's? Their value alone is too little, because together they do more than apart. Their added value when they join depends on who is already there: the second engineer adds less than the first. Lloyd Shapley's answer is to imagine the group forming one person at a time, in every possible order, and to give each person their added value averaged over all those orders.

The Shapley value is the only way of dividing a joint value that satisfies four reasonable conditions: someone who never adds anything gets nothing; two people who always add the same get the same; the whole value is shared out; and values add up across separate games. Page shows it at work in a creativity test, where it amounts to splitting the credit for each idea equally among everyone who thought of it.

## Formulation

::: {.model-box}
**Cooperative game.** A set $N$ of players and a value function $V$ that gives every coalition $S \subseteq N$ a value $V(S)$, with $V(\varnothing) = 0$; $V(N)$ is the total value of the game.

**Shapley value.** Consider all $|N|!$ orders in which the players could join. Player $i$'s added value in an ordering is $V(\text{those before } i \cup \{i\}) - V(\text{those before } i)$. Then

$$
\phi_i = \frac{1}{|N|!} \sum_{\text{orderings}} \Big[ V\big(P_i \cup \{i\}\big) - V(P_i) \Big]
= \sum_{S \subseteq N \setminus \{i\}} \frac{|S|!\,(|N| - |S| - 1)!}{|N|!} \Big[ V(S \cup \{i\}) - V(S) \Big],
$$

where $P_i$ is the set of players who come before $i$.

**Result.** The Shapley value is the unique allocation satisfying the zero property, symmetry (fairness), full allocation ($\sum_i \phi_i = V(N)$) and additivity.
:::

## Interactive model

Three founders, an engineer (A), a designer (B) and a marketer (C), can each build something alone or together. Set what each coalition would be worth. The table lists all six orders in which the team could have formed and each founder's added value; the Shapley value is the average of each column. Compare it with an equal split.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {C, fmt} from "../js/models.js"
```

```{ojs}
viewof game = Inputs.form({
  A: Inputs.range([0, 100], {value: 10, step: 5, label: "V(A)"}),
  B: Inputs.range([0, 100], {value: 0, step: 5, label: "V(B)"}),
  C: Inputs.range([0, 100], {value: 0, step: 5, label: "V(C)"}),
  AB: Inputs.range([0, 150], {value: 60, step: 5, label: "V(A, B)"}),
  AC: Inputs.range([0, 150], {value: 40, step: 5, label: "V(A, C)"}),
  BC: Inputs.range([0, 150], {value: 10, step: 5, label: "V(B, C)"}),
  ABC: Inputs.range([0, 200], {value: 100, step: 5, label: "V(A, B, C)"})
})
```

```{ojs}
shapley = {
  const V = s => (s.length === 0 ? 0 : game[[...s].sort().join("")]);
  const perms = [["A","B","C"], ["A","C","B"], ["B","A","C"], ["B","C","A"], ["C","A","B"], ["C","B","A"]];
  const rows = perms.map(order => {
    const row = {Order: order.join(" → ")}, before = [];
    for (const p of order) { row[p] = V([...before, p]) - V(before); before.push(p); }
    return row;
  });
  const phi = {A: 0, B: 0, C: 0};
  for (const r of rows) for (const p of "ABC") phi[p] += r[p] / 6;
  return {rows, phi};
}
```

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(shapley.rows, {columns: ["Order", "A", "B", "C"], header: {A: "A adds", B: "B adds", C: "C adds"}, rows: 7, layout: "auto"})
```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  ariaLabel: "Shapley Value: shares of the joint value",
  ariaDescription: "Grouped bars for each founder: their Shapley value (teal) and an equal split of the total (gray). The summary below the chart states the result in words.",
  height: 220,
  fx: {label: null, domain: ["A (engineer)", "B (designer)", "C (marketer)"]},
  x: {axis: null, domain: ["Shapley value", "Equal split"]},
  y: {label: "Share of V(A, B, C)", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["Shapley value", "Equal split"], range: [C.teal, C.gray]},
  marks: [
    Plot.barY(["A", "B", "C"].flatMap(p => [
      {who: {A: "A (engineer)", B: "B (designer)", C: "C (marketer)"}[p], kind: "Shapley value", v: shapley.phi[p]},
      {who: {A: "A (engineer)", B: "B (designer)", C: "C (marketer)"}[p], kind: "Equal split", v: game.ABC / 3}
    ]), {fx: "who", x: "kind", y: "v", fill: "kind"}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
})
```

## R {.unlisted}

```{.r}
# Shapley value of a three-player cooperative game, over all orderings.
# Deterministic: no random numbers.
v <- c(
  A = 10, B = 0, C = 0, AB = 60, AC = 40, BC = 10, ABC = 100
)
value <- function(players) {
  if (length(players) == 0) {
    return(0)
  }
  v[[paste(sort(players), collapse = "")]]
}

orders <- list(
  c("A", "B", "C"), c("A", "C", "B"), c("B", "A", "C"),
  c("B", "C", "A"), c("C", "A", "B"), c("C", "B", "A")
)
added <- t(sapply(orders, function(o) {
  out <- c(A = 0, B = 0, C = 0)
  for (k in seq_along(o)) {
    out[o[k]] <- value(o[1:k]) - value(o[seq_len(k - 1)])
  }
  out
}))
rownames(added) <- sapply(orders, paste, collapse = "")
print(added)
phi <- colMeans(added)
cat("Shapley values:", round(phi, 2), " total:", sum(phi), "\n")

barplot(phi, col = "#148a91", ylab = "Shapley value")
abline(h = v[["ABC"]] / 3, lty = 2)
```

:::

</details>

## Takeaways

::: takeaways
- A player's contribution depends on who else is there; the Shapley value averages it over every order of arrival.
- It is the unique division of a joint value satisfying zero property, symmetry, full allocation and additivity.
- Credit for a shared idea is split equally among the people who had it; unique contributions earn full credit.
:::

## Uses

::: uses
- **Design.** Divide profits among partners, costs among users of shared infrastructure, or credit among features of a machine-learning model (SHAP values).
- **Reason.** Distinguish a person's standalone value from the value they add to a team.
- **Explain.** Why someone with fewer but more unusual ideas can contribute more to a group than someone with many common ones.
:::
